description: Finding types and the triage() result of soar/core/attack.py; asserted by pytest (test_export_attack_table.py) and Jest (docs-api soc tests).

expected.impact: Instance-role credentials were used from outside AWS: the attacker held the report-worker's permissions until the sessions were revoked.
eradication: Confirm the revoke-older-sessions deny is on the instance role (PB-01).
Find the IMDS access path (SSRF or a shell) on the instance from the EBS snapshot.
Enforce IMDSv2 with hop limit 1 on the launch template.
Review CloudTrail for every call made with the stolen session.
recovery: Replace the quarantined instance from a clean launch template (ADR-0003).
Remove the quarantine NACL entries only after the replacement is healthy.
Keep the snapshot and manifest until the case is closed.

Check the scanned targets' logs for follow-up connections.

expected.impact: A long-term IAM access key was used by an untrusted caller.
eradication: Confirm the key is Inactive and the session-revocation deny is on the user (PB-02).
Find where the key leaked (repository, CI log, workstation) and purge it.
Review CloudTrail for every call made with the key.
recovery: Delete the deactivated key once the investigation no longer needs it.
Issue a replacement credential only if the user still needs one (prefer a role).

expected.impact: A project bucket's public-access protection was disabled: its objects may have been readable.
eradication: Confirm all four Block Public Access flags are on (PB-03 read-back).
Review S3 data events for anonymous GetObject during the exposure window.
Codify the block in Terraform (the report adds a ready-to-apply block when PB-03 recorded a valid bucket name) so drift is visible.
recovery: Remove or rewrite the bucket policy statements that granted public access.
Rotate any secret that was stored in the exposed objects.

eradication: Review the finding in GuardDuty and decide whether it is a true positive.
recovery: Record the outcome on the incident before closing it.

expected.impact: Unexpected code ran inside an application container. Containment stopped the task and redeployed the service from the SAME image digest (D12).
eradication: Capture volatile state with ECS Exec from a sibling task BEFORE approving eradication (the runbook's human step).
Build and scan a new image; deploy it by digest. Replacements of a compromised image are compromised too.
Review the task-definition environment and task role for exposed secrets.
recovery: Confirm the new deployment is PRIMARY and healthy.
Keep the PB-04 prestate evidence object for the case (docs/runbooks/pb04-pb05-recovery.md).

expected.impact: A client exceeded the edge rate limit or hit a decoy route: probing or abuse of the public app.
eradication: Review WAF logs (query 04) for the client's URIs and terminating rules.
Check the application audit trail for requests from the address that succeeded.
recovery: The PB-05 sweeper lifts the block automatically once blockExpiresAt has passed (D15); tools/list_expired_blocks.py cross-checks expired, lost and orphan entries.
Lift it early by hand if the address is shared (NAT, carrier gateway) or a false positive (docs/runbooks/pb04-pb05-recovery.md).
